value.pricing.line_total(sku, qty, customer_id: -> float dollars = round(qty*unit_price*(1-discount), 2); None if sku or customer unknown
value.tax needs: category and region come from the item/customer dicts; tax.py takes the taxable amount (float dollars) plus category and region

why: Initial API proposal for pricing.py. Data is stored in cents; converted to dollars at the boundary per team standard. Discounts stored as fractions per team standard. None signals not-found.

value.region: str or None. Customer region code as in data_tax/rates.csv (e.g. TX). None = unknown customer, pays 0 tax. A non-None region missing from rates.csv raises KeyError.
value.lines: list of dicts {"category": str, "amount_cents": int}. amount_cents = line total in integer cents (quantity already multiplied in). Lines whose category is listed in exempt_categories.csv are not taxed.
value.discount_pct: percent number (10 means 10%). Applied to the taxable sum: base = taxable_sum * (100 - discount_pct) / 100.
value.returns: int, tax in integer cents. tax = base * rate_pct / 100, computed with exact arithmetic and rounded once, half up, to the nearest cent. Not a float.
value.other: tax.py also exposes tax_rate_pct(region) -> number (KeyError if region unknown; None -> 0) and is_exempt(category) -> bool. Both are optional for others to use.

why: Defines the tax interface so pricing and invoice can call it. Uses team standard units: integer cents, percent numbers, KeyError on unknown lookup. Explicit exception: an unknown customer (region None) pays 0 per RULES.md, because RULES.md calls for it. Rounding is applied once at the end to avoid double rounding.

value.pricing.get_unit_price: get_unit_price(sku) -> Decimal dollars; Decimal(0) if sku unknown
value.pricing.get_customer_name: get_customer_name(customer_id) -> str; empty string if unknown (invoice then shows the id)
value.pricing.get_discount_multiplier: get_discount_multiplier(customer_id) -> Decimal; 0.90 for 10% off; Decimal(1) for no discount or unknown customer (exception to the default-0 rule, since 0 would mean 100% off)
value.tax.compute_tax: compute_tax(customer_id, lines, discount) -> (tax_amount Decimal quantized to 0.01 half-up, tax_multiplier Decimal e.g. 1.0825). lines = list of (sku, line_amount Decimal) for known skus only, in order; discount = Decimal dollars subtracted from subtotal. tax.py decides the taxable base (per-sku taxability and discount handling). Unknown customer -> (Decimal 0.00, Decimal 1)

why: agent3 (invoice) proposal: pricing and tax expose only data and rules, invoice does arithmetic and formatting. Open to changes.
Matches the example: taxable base = 2500 cents (A) * 0.90 = 2250 -> 185.625 -> 186 cents = $1.86, so D must be exempt. Invoice converts cents to Decimal internally.

(1) line_total applies the discount per line; the spec applies discount to the invoice subtotal (39.10 * 10% = 3.91). Per-line rounding gives 35.19 instead, so pricing must return raw unit prices only. (2) Use the same units as tax_api: integer cents (unit_price_cents) and discount_pct as a percent number (10 = 10%). (3) get_item must include category, which tax needs.

value.units: integer cents for money (unit_price_cents), percent numbers for discounts (discount_pct: 10 means 10%); matches tax_api. Lookups that find nothing return None.
value.pricing.get_item(sku): -> {"sku": str, "name": str, "unit_price_cents": int, "category": str} or None. Raw unit price only; no discount, no quantity.
value.pricing.get_customer(customer_id): -> {"id": str, "name": str, "discount_pct": number, "region": str} or None. region is the code used by tax_api (e.g. TX).
value.discount: pricing does NOT apply discounts to lines. Invoice applies discount_pct to the subtotal (e.g. 3910 cents * 10 / 100) and passes it to tax_api as discount_pct. Pricing does no arithmetic beyond returning stored values.
value.unknown customer: get_customer returns None; invoice treats it as no discount, and tax_api gets region None.
